answer: Cross-graph audit watermarking. Each transaction embeds a per-epoch lotus marker keyed to the submitter's derived identity hash; auditors later sample subgraphs and test whether marker reuse forms clusters denser than chance, flagging linked accounts. A lone honest marker looks like ordinary noise, but a false vertex reuse across many accounts leaves a detectable pigment of shared origin. Attackers pay by needing unique, uncorrelated markers per fake identity, forcing costly per-account key derivation and defeating cheap bulk registration.
